title: skill_state
description: One row per (user, capability) over the 74 capabilities in corpus/capabilities/registry.json — the SKILL track, deliberately not FSRS. Its signal is binary and capability-level, so a 21-parameter model would fit noise; a bounded-ease ladder is robust, explainable and cheap (design/srs_design.md §5). RUNTIME class: minted per learner, never committed to this repo. See design/user_state.md §8.

x-yomineko.note: Capabilities are skills, not memories. Scheduling them with FSRS was considered and rejected on granularity: the exam feed would double-count against the memory track.

capability.description: The capability, by stable id — something the learner can DO once a set of lessons is complete.

ease.description: SM-2-flavoured ease. Correct: +0.06, capped at 3.0. Incorrect: -0.25, floored at 1.3. The floor and the cap are both load-bearing — the cap is what keeps even a mastered capability resurfacing.

streak.description: Consecutive correct answers. Drives the interval: round(ease^streak) days, capped at 21. Reset to 0 on an incorrect answer, whose interval is 1 day.

due_at.description: Never zeroed out: even an ease-3.0 capability comes back at least every 21 days.

last_result.description: The signal is binary by design. Null before the first answer. Vocabulary owner: design — design/user_state.md#8-skill_state. Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

correct.description: With `reps`, the denominator behind any "you are weak at X" claim shown to the learner.

recent_items.description: The no-repeat window: an item drilled for this capability may not return for 10 sessions (design/srs_design.md §2). Bounded at 10 on purpose — it is state, not a log, and a log of drilled items belongs nowhere near a row read on every queue build.
